change: First end-to-end run of rules + gap logic with perfect extraction
finding: 344 facts dropped: short answers such as 'No.' fail the quote check (too short to verify) and get re-asked, inflating redundant questions. Over-tiering: chatbots that 'answer on their own' fired the Bank rule for acting on customers without review; customer-call emotion detection fired the workplace prohibition because the text mentioned 'agents'.

change: Accept short quotes only when they answer the question just asked about that field; restrict the acts-without-review rule to decision domains or explicit block/decline wording; workplace emotion recognition requires employment domain or emotion-of-staff wording
finding: Drops fixed. Redundancy rose because the synthetic briefs contained bare 'No.' sentences that are meaningless out of context (a data problem, not a system problem). The acts-without-review regex still matched 'answers ... without human review'.

change: Rewrite bare yes/no facts as self-contained sentences in the generator; acts-without-review regex requires an action verb (block, decline, restrict, approve...); customer-facing detection reads the team's quote, not only the boolean
finding: 'Personal financial data' matched the credit pattern 'personal financ...' so a voice bot and a savings chatbot became high risk.

change: Credit pattern tightened to 'personal loan/financing'. Rules frozen (git commit 2fc5493).
finding: 100% on the cases the rules were tuned on is not evidence of generalisation. A held-out set of 14 new cases was written after the freeze.

Overfitting confirmed: 100% -> 71% on unseen wording. X6: 'digitally manipulated video' (deepfake detection) fired Art. 5(1)(a) manipulation. X11: 'people recruited as mules' fired the employment rule. X14: a document checklist on 'personal financing applications' fired credit scoring. X8 and X11 need model screening (external content; Bank prohibited use), which the oracle does not do. Not fixed: reported as a known limitation so the held-out numbers stay honest.
